question.text: This Irish political figure avoided being executed following the Easter Rising, and opposed the Anglo-Irish Treaty; he would later serve as President of Ireland until his death in 1975.
question.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

swap.leadin: This party's name means "Ours Alone" or "We Ourselves."
swap.text: Name this political party, which does not sit in the British Parliament, founded by Arthur Griffith. This Irish Republican political party was once led by Gerry Adams as well as former IRA leader Martin McGuinness.
swap.clue: Former Tanaiste Eamon Gilmore was originally a member of this party before eventually joining the Labour Party.

question.leadin: This organization agreed to disarm in the Good Friday Agreement, which ended a decades-long conflict known as The Troubles.
question.text: Name this paramilitary organization which conducted bombings and assassinations in Northern Ireland in the late 20th century.
question.answerHtml: IRA [or Irish Republican Army; or the Provisional Irish Republican Army]
question.clue: This group fought the Black and Tans during a war of independence when they were supported by a political party called "we ourselves," or Sinn Fein .

swap.leadin: Douglas Hyde and Patrick Pearse were members of a League founded in 1893 to promote a language known by this term.
swap.text: Name this cultural term, which underwent a "revival" in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.
swap.answerHtml: Gaelic [accept Gaeilge; or the Gaelic Revival; prompt on Irish or Celtic]
swap.clue: This cultural term, which underwent a "revival" in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.

question.leadin: Eoin ("owen") MacNeill gave orders to halt mobilization in this event, but Patrick Pearse (peers) and Tom Clarke continued anyway.
question.text: Name this rebellion, which began with a raid on the General Post Office. Roger Casement asked for German aid for this event and was later executed for his participation.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter uprising or Easter Rebellion or Éirí Amach na Cásca or Éirí Amach 1916 or Aiséirí na Cásca; prompt on Easter or Easter 1916 or the Rising]
question.clue: Liberty Hall was captured by a volunteer force during this event, which failed partly due to the interception of a shipment of German arms.

swap.leadin: This nation held a referendum in May 2015 that approved same-sex marriage, the first nation to do so.
swap.text: Name this largely Catholic European country.
swap.clue: Its war for independence is known as the Black and Tan War, and the Battle of the Boyne was fought in this nation.

question.leadin: Isaac Butt founded a "League" to promote this political cause, which was the goal of two bills introduced to the House of Commons by William Gladstone.
question.text: Name this specific form of Irish self-government, which is distinct from independence. Between about 1870 and 1920, it was popular among nationalists and some British Liberals but generally opposed by Unionists.
question.clue: Edward Carson and James Craig, leaders of the Unionists, campaigned against a 1914 bill aiming to bring about this outcome.

swap.text: Parnell's career was earlier threatened by forged letters connecting him to the Phoenix Park Murders in this city, which has served as the capital of Ireland since its independence.
swap.clue: This city's King Imar was likely the same person as Ragnar Lodbrok's son Ivar the Boneless.

question.leadin: Name these members of the Irish Republican Army.
question.text: This IRA intelligence director worked with Arthur Griffith to negotiate the 1921 treaty creating the Irish Republic, though IRA hardliners were dissatisfied with the terms.
question.clue: This leader of an assassination group known as The Squad was imprisoned at Frongoch internment camp for their role as aide-de-camp to Joseph Plunkett during the Easter Rising.

swap.text: This leader of the Land League gave the speech that incited the original boycott. As an MP, he convinced members of the Liberal Party to support Irish Home Rule.
swap.clue: From jail, this man negotiated an agreement with William Gladstone that included concessions for land tenants called the Kilmainham Treaty.

question.text: This member of the IRA was elected as a member of Parliament while he was in prison. He died in Maze Prison less than a month after his election as part of the 1981 Irish hunger strike.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.text: In response to the Irish Republican Army's assassination of former Viceroy of India Louis Mountbatten, this politician asserted Mountbatten "knew the danger" involved in coming to Ireland could possibly lead to his "execution." This man served as the leader of Sinn Fein ("shin fayn") from 1983 until 2018.
swap.clue: In interviews for an oral history project conducted by Boston College, Brendan Hughes and Dolours Price implicated this person in the murder of Jean McConville.

question.text: All six prime ministers of Northern Ireland belonged to this political party, which dominated Unionist politics after partition.
question.clue: With John Hume of the SDLP, this party's leader won the 1998 Nobel Peace Prize for facilitating the Good Friday Agreement.

swap.text: In 1918, MacNeill was elected to the first meeting of this legislature. This legislature ruled over Ireland in opposition to British rule from 1919 to 1922, during Ireland's revolutionary period.

question.leadin: "'God save Ireland!' said the heroes / 'God save Ireland' said they all." Answer the following about Irish rebel music.
question.text: Dominic Behan's song "Come Out Ye [these people]" asks them to tell their wives "...how the IRA made you run like hell away / from the green and lovely lanes of Killeshandra." This notoriously brutal auxiliary force opened fire at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.
question.clue: The first man they formally executed was Kevin Barry, whom they captured on the same day as their sack of Balbriggan.

swap.leadin: A song called about this event is called "The Fields of Athenry."
swap.text: Name this 1840s, event which saw a particular island's population drop by almost twenty-five percent due to death and immigration, all due to the failure of a crucial crop.
swap.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine [accept equivalents if they have Ireland and Potato; prompt on partial answers; accept Gorta Mor]
swap.clue: The Baring Brothers and Company ordered shipments of corn in response to this event, but other relief efforts were stopped by Charles Trevelyan, who attributed this event to divine judgment.

question.leadin: Settlers in this region included wealthy "Undertakers" and war veterans called "Servitors."
question.text: Name this region whose "plantation" during James I's reign began after a failed rebellion in the Nine Years' War. The "Flight of the Earls" from this region marked the end of its old order.
question.answerHtml: Ulster [or Ulaidh or Cúige Uladh or Ulstèr; accept “Plantation of Ulster”; prompt on Ireland or Éire or Airlann]
question.clue: This region was the center of the Flight of the Earls that escaped from Oriel and Tyrconnell which were both in this region.

swap.leadin: This man supposedly stated that "England has had its luckiest escape since the Armada" after his invading fleet was dispersed by a storm in Bantry Bay.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Society of United Irishmen who allied with France's Committee of Public Safety to liberate Ireland. He was sentenced to death but either committed suicide or was tortured to death before his execution.
swap.clue: In 1796, Hoche led an unsuccessful expedition to assist this rebel's United Irishmen. This Protestant lawyer names a band that recorded "Come Out Ye Black and Tans."

question.leadin: Answer the following about a Dark Age saint.
question.text: Seventh century biographers Tirechan and Muirchu tell tales of his hostility to the Druids. More reliable is the humble rustic Latin of his own "Confession."
question.clue: This Christian saint who, according to legend, taught the Trinity using a shamrock and exiled all snakes from the isle where he preached, Ireland.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a brief period in which religious factionalism was set aside in Ireland, only to have lofty goals dashed and much blood spilt.
swap.text: One major goal of the United Irishmen was the repeal of these discriminatory laws, which prevented Irish Catholics from holding public office and severely restricted their right to inherit land.
swap.clue: The vicar proved his loyalty to James II by "shout[ing] down" laws of this type, exemplified by the Clarendon Code and the Test Acts that prohibited Catholics from holding office. A similar set of laws were enacted in Ireland.
